latest_completed_work.title: Complete remaining post-launch security and maintenance gates

active_work_item.goal: No queued launch or post-launch remediation remains. Resume only for new evidence, dependency maintenance, or a newly approved product/operations change.

PR #384 updated deploy-pages to v5.0.1 and the resulting GitHub Pages Production deployment completed successfully. #350 and #366 were closed as documented v1 accepted residuals; stale PRs #294 and #356 were closed.
known_non_blockers: Issue #348 is complete: 30-day-grace bounded cleanup is deployed, the first Production preview found zero eligible rows in all five target categories, and recurring bounded cleanup is configured. No first-run DB deletion was necessary.

PR #384 updated actions/deploy-pages to v5.0.1 on current main; exact-head PR Verify, Browser Smoke, CodeQL, Pre-Live Safety, and Claude Code Review all passed, and the subsequent Production Pages deployment succeeded.
Issue #350 is closed as not planned for v1: meaningful frontend security headers require a broader hosting/CDN/DNS change; meta-only substitutes remain intentionally rejected.
Issue #366 is closed as not planned for v1: public/static premium-asset extraction remains an accepted commercial residual unless product value or piracy risk materially changes.
PR #294 was superseded and closed; the complete GitHub Agentic Workflow implementation already merged via PR #296.

Issue #351 remains resolved: nonexistent Tamamizu API paths return 404 while auth capabilities returns 200, signed-out auth/me returns 401, ops remains 403, and the parent WordPress site remains healthy.

Security Audit v1 Production cutover remains complete: migrations 0008/0009 applied, matching reviewed backend deployed, release integrity passed, and Paddle reconciliation finished with zero unresolved blocks.

Production Email OTP, exact Production CORS, real-device auth persistence/logout QA, cancelled-checkout UX, one real Paddle purchase, and one real refund were already validated; do not repeat them for routine confidence.

Revisit a hosting/CDN migration for stronger frontend response headers when there is a broader hosting reason to do so.
